coverage_gaps: Handler-lock extraction parsed 2317 irq registrations in s08 and resolved in-file lock usage for the 185 handlers that take at least one plain spin_lock; handlers defined in other files, macro-declared, or registered via function pointers were not resolved or examined.

Cross-indexing matched lock expressions textually (base name) within the registering file only, so locks shared across files via exported helpers or spelled differently (&priv->lock vs &dev->lock aliases) could be missed.
request_threaded_irq registrations were not split into primary hardirq handler vs thread_fn; thread-context acquisitions of primary-handler-shared locks were not separately audited.

Deep caller-context tracing was completed only for the four reported files (korg1212, synclink_gt, ens1370, mtk_star_emac); the remaining cross.tsv top rows (zs.c, isp1760-udc, mv_u3d, net2280, nhi, goku_udc, m66592, net2272, ipu_idmac, fec_mpc52xx, ravb, fotg210, fusb300, winbond-840, defxx, mps2-uart, pmac_zilog, samsung_tty, stm32-usart, dbri, ni_pcidio, k3-udma, psb_irq, ite-cir, altera_tse, bcm63xx_enet, gemini, sundance, atp, defza, skfddi and serial drivers) were classified from the cross-index table and targeted greps only, without full context tracing.

Legacy s08 softirq-branch facts (f011 xmit-softirq mwl8k, f027 timer-dwork cxgb4/hdlc_cisco, f037 tasklet-NAPI fs_enet/altera_tse/cassini) were consulted to avoid duplication; no systematic union of their lock sets with the hardirq handler lock sets was performed beyond the overlapping files handled.
limitations: All four findings are static hypotheses; no kernel build or runtime reproducer was executed (the tree lacks a .config and the snapshot is read-only), so the deadlock path is argued from source context alone.

Function-boundary attribution in the scan uses a naive line-based parser; handler-internal acquisitions were spot-verified by direct reads for the reported files, but the cross.tsv line numbers for unresolved candidates are approximate and must be re-verified before use.

For the reported audio/tty cases the harmful direction requires the IRQ to fire on the same CPU as the preempted process-context holder; on non-shared IRQs with strict per-CPU affinity this is the common case but was not measured.
The mtk_star_emac case depends on NAPI poll being preempted by the RX/TX-complete hardirq on the same CPU; IRQ affinity steering or threaded-NAPI configurations could narrow the window.
